title: Base change morphism for etale extension by zero
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $j:V\to X$ be an etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism], and let $V'=Y\times_XV$ be the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $j':V'\to Y$ and $f':V'\to V$, so $f\circ j'=j\circ f'$, and $j'$ is etale as a base change of $j$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]; let $\square=(f,f',j,j',\mathrm{id})$ be this cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] (top $j'$, bottom $j$). Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the category of sheaves of $\Lambda_T$-modules on the small etale site of a scheme $T$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use: the extensions by zero $j_!:\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $j'_!:\Mod(V'_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] with the adjunctions $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$, $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives]; the inverse and direct images of sheaves of modules with the adjunctions $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$, $f'^{-1}\dashv f'_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; the composite adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]
$$
 L_1=f^{-1}\circ j_!\ \dashv\ R_1=j^{-1}\circ f_*,\qquad L_2=j'_!\circ f'^{-1}\ \dashv\ R_2=f'_*\circ j'^{-1}
$$
(functors $\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)\rightleftarrows\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$), with units $\eta_1,\eta_2$ and counits $\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_2$; and the underived exchange transformation $\Ex^0_\square:R_1=j^{-1}f_*\to f'_*j'^{-1}=R_2$ of $\square$ [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], a natural transformation of functors $\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-module-linear].

The *base change morphism for extension by zero* of $\square$ is the natural transformation
$$
 \beta=\beta_\square:\ j'_!\circ f'^{-1}=L_2\longrightarrow L_1=f^{-1}\circ j_!
$$
of functors $\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ whose conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] with respect to $L_1\dashv R_1$ and $L_2\dashv R_2$ is $\Ex^0_\square$: $\beta^c=\Ex^0_\square$; it exists and is unique because $\tau\mapsto\tau^c$ is a bijection [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Explicitly, for $M\in\Mod(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$,
$$
 \beta_M:\ j'_!f'^{-1}M\xrightarrow{L_2(\eta_{1,M})}L_2R_1L_1M\xrightarrow{L_2(\Ex^0_{\square,L_1M})}L_2R_2L_1M\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{2,L_1M}}L_1M=f^{-1}j_!M,
$$
i.e. $\beta_M$ is the morphism corresponding under the hom bijection of $L_2\dashv R_2$ to $\Ex^0_{\square,L_1M}\circ\eta_{1,M}:M\to R_1L_1M\to R_2L_1M$, where $\eta_{1,M}=j^{-1}(\eta_{f,j_!M})\circ\eta_{j,M}$. It is natural in $M$. (Stacks Project, Etale Cohomology, Lemma 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change) identifies $j'_!f'^{-1}$ with $f^{-1}j_!$ by comparing the right adjoints $f'_*(j')^{-1}$ and $j^{-1}f_*$; $\beta$ is the comparison morphism of left adjoints so obtained. It runs from $j'_!f'^{-1}$ to $f^{-1}j_!$, against the direction of an exchange morphism, as the base change map of the source repository does for open immersions.)
